BiblicalUsage: This verb for grappling or wrestling occurs only at the Jabbok, in Genesis 32:24-25: 'there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh.' It is the close, dusty struggle of two men locked together in the dark.
TheologicalSignificance: Jacob wrestled all night and came away limping and blessed — the wound and the blessing in the same encounter. I believe God sometimes meets us this way: not with an answer handed over, but with a struggle that leaves us changed, and a limp that reminds us who won.
